title: EOS: An Energy-Oriented Attack Framework for Spiking Neural Networks
problem: SNNs are vulnerable to parameter-level attacks via malicious bit-flips in DRAM memory storing neuronal information, a security threat largely unexplored compared to adversarial input attacks. The specific challenge is identifying which neuronal parameters to target to maximize energy consumption while preserving accuracy.
motivation: As SNNs are increasingly deployed in energy-constrained edge devices, understanding parameter-level security vulnerabilities is essential to prevent malicious energy amplification attacks that could compromise device reliability.
method: EOS employs the Row Hammer technique to induce bit-flips in DRAM where SNN neuronal parameters are stored. It analyzes spiking activity to identify robust neurons, targeting firing threshold parameters encoded as binary bits. A progressive search strategy systematically identifies bit-flip positions that maximize energy consumption while maintaining task accuracy.
key_novelty: Targeting SNN firing threshold parameters via Row Hammer bit-flips guided by spiking activity patterns to achieve significant energy amplification while preserving model accuracy.
contributions: Novel EOS attack framework demonstrating critical parameter-level vulnerabilities in SNNs
Spiking activity-based neuron selection methodology for identifying optimal attack targets
Progressive search strategy for energy-maximizing bit-flip placement
Empirical demonstration of 43% energy increase with zero accuracy loss
limitations: The paper does not discuss practical constraints of Row Hammer exploitability on modern systems with mitigations, assumptions about memory layout and access patterns, or generalization across diverse SNN architectures.
primary_theme: Parameter-level adversarial attacks via memory bit-flips
